newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank seeks 40 bln peso more capital.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank seeks 40 bln peso more capital.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson urged the Lower House on Wednesday to pass a resolution that will provide the Central Bank with an additional 40 billion pesos in capitalization.
The additional capital is needed to pursue effective monetary and reserve management, he said in a Congressional hearing.

He noted that under the law which created a new Central Bank in 1993, the Central Bank should have capital of 50 billion pesos within a period of two years and said that only 10 billion pesos has so far been paid by the national government.

To pay for the increased capital, the Central Bank chief proposed that Congress authorize the government to convert 40 billion pesos of its 50 billion-peso special deposit with the Central Bank into equity since the deposit cannot be used by the government until 2003.

"The additional 40 billion pesos can be done by Congress without having to go through the tedious budgetary process, and without the national government having to raise additional revenues to fund it," Singson said.

Considering the magnitude of the Central Bank's responsibility, the Central Bank's current capital is small when compared to four banks in the country which had paid-up capital each of ten billion pesos and more at the end of 1996, he said.
Separately, a Finance department official told Reuters a separate appropriation law would have to be passed even if the law creating the new Central Bank specified a 50 billion-peso capital.
Likewise, a law may also have to be passed, instead of a Congressional resolution, for the conversion of the government deposits in Central Bank into equity, he said.

The conversion of these deposits into equity may result in foregone revenues for the government of four billion pesos yearly from interest income. But these could also be offset by higher dividends that the Central Bank may remit to the government, he said.
